validations: AC-02: validate protected requirement — Every new candidate is non-runtime and non-executable until explicit approval/admission. Discovery never returns an admitted/runtime skill by side effect.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — Tier A/B/C/D and provenance states are deterministic. Curated-only/unknown upstream cannot satisfy automatic-admission provenance.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — License state is explicit. `UNKNOWN` is not treated as allowed; prohibited license state blocks admission.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Focused/adversarial fixtures detect generic execution/network, credential handling, policy-bypass and unauthorized production/destructive claims without executing candidate content.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Tests prove intake never invokes subprocess/shell/package install/MCP start/raw HTTP/browser execution from candidate instructions.
AC-07: validate protected requirement — Exact replay is idempotent. Same upstream/version with changed material digest produces explicit conflict/HUMAN_REQUIRED or BLOCKED, never replacement.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — Successful admission calls/uses existing `SkillRegistry.admit`; unapproved/tampered/undeclarable contracts retain existing failure semantics.
AC-10: validate protected requirement — Tool candidates and skill-required capability declarations cannot construct, approve, enable or mutate `ToolCapability` authority in S2.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Runtime retrieval exposes admitted skills only and final deterministic choice remains the existing `SkillSelector`, including HUMAN_REQUIRED on missing capability/incompatible repository/ambiguity.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Catalog/operator output contains bounded metadata/reason codes/digests but no raw secrets, unrestricted source bodies, executable handles, hidden reasoning or provider credentials.
AC-13: validate protected requirement — Global catalog cannot accept Project-private source/evidence as reusable public candidate material without an explicit future protected policy.
AC-14: validate protected requirement — Source observations can be supplied through a bounded adapter/interface and tested without granting live arbitrary network authority.
AC-15: validate protected requirement — Existing governed-skill tests, tool capability authority tests, provider/browser authority tests and full API regressions remain green.

AC-17: validate protected requirement — Final implementation head passes focused tests, Workstream Spec Validation, P2 CI, Bounded Autonomy and applicable protected release gates. Changed production components are deployment-verified before recorded as deployed.

AC-18: validate protected requirement — When the S2 contract is accepted/released, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CURRENT-STATE.md` are updated because this introduces a durable supply-chain/capability architecture. `PROJECT-CONSTITUTION.md` changes only if existing security/human-control principles prove insufficient. `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` changes only if a user-facing capability-management surface establishes durable new presentation rules.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Canonical candidate identity
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Candidate identity is bounded, deterministic and changes when material source/version/content facts change.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Quarantine by default
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Every new candidate is non-runtime and non-executable until explicit approval/admission. Discovery never returns an admitted/runtime skill by side effect.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Source-tier/provenance semantics
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Tier A/B/C/D and provenance states are deterministic. Curated-only/unknown upstream cannot satisfy automatic-admission provenance.

protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Exact replay is idempotent. Same upstream/version with changed material digest produces explicit conflict/HUMAN_REQUIRED or BLOCKED, never replacement.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Explicit approval identity

protected_acceptance_map.title: Existing registry remains authoritative
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Successful admission calls/uses existing `SkillRegistry.admit`; unapproved/tampered/undeclarable contracts retain existing failure semantics.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Tool authority separation
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Tool candidates and skill-required capability declarations cannot construct, approve, enable or mutate `ToolCapability` authority in S2.

protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Runtime retrieval exposes admitted skills only and final deterministic choice remains the existing `SkillSelector`, including HUMAN_REQUIRED on missing capability/incompatible repository/ambiguity.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Safe serialization
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Catalog/operator output contains bounded metadata/reason codes/digests but no raw secrets, unrestricted source bodies, executable handles, hidden reasoning or provider credentials.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Public/private isolation

protected_acceptance_map.title: No regression of current skills/tools
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Existing governed-skill tests, tool capability authority tests, provider/browser authority tests and full API regressions remain green.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Authentic DSPy gate
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Authentic DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler evidence for this exact spec is committed and protected `--require-dspy` validation passes before semantic implementation. Any temporary workflow/evidence-generation change is restored byte-for-byte before implementation qualification.

protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Final implementation head passes focused tests, Workstream Spec Validation, P2 CI, Bounded Autonomy and applicable protected release gates. Changed production components are deployment-verified before recorded as deployed.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Durable-record reconciliation
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: When the S2 contract is accepted/released, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CURRENT-STATE.md` are updated because this introduces a durable supply-chain/capability architecture. `PROJECT-CONSTITUTION.md` changes only if existing security/human-control principles prove insufficient. `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` changes only if a user-facing capability-management surface establishes durable new presentation rules.

critique: The first accepted slice must turn bounded external-source metadata and inspected candidate content into deterministic, replay-safe quarantined candidate records, explain trust/admission state, and bridge an explicitly approved exact Parallax skill contract into the existing `SkillRegistry` without changing the existing deterministic `SkillSelector` or Project-scoped `ToolCapabilityRegistry` authority model.
